messages:
maria: Heads-up — after landing asymmetric-int8 quant for the new reranker v2, we see a ~6% MRR drop on prod-like holdout. NDCG@10 mostly unchanged. Anyone else see this?

dan: saw the CI alerts, interesting that NDCG stable but MRR down. can you share the holdout cohort + eval command?

maria: short summary: holdout=recent-week sampled users, 10 candidates, candidate order preserved. Eval command: `python eval_rerank.py --model rerank-v2-asym8 --holdout s3://redwood/evals/holdout-week.json --metrics mrr ndcg@10` — I'll paste logs in a sec

alex: quick q — did quantization change tokenizer params or truncation? tokenization shifts cause rank changes all the time

maria: tokenizer same checksum, but we switched to concat-with-sep that could alter doc boundaries. I'll diff a sample.

sophia: also check candidate ordering — are you shuffling before scoring? MRR sensitive to ties and ordering.

maria: no shuffle; used preserved ordering. here's a failing example (ids redacted):
```
query: "how to rotate logs"
cands:
  - docA (score 0.93)
  - docB (score 0.90)
  - docC (score 0.89)
label: docB
```
On float32 docB ranks 1, whereas asym8 ranks docA above docB

dan: could be score quantization resolution collapsing near-ties. what's the score histogram delta? plot quant - float

maria: attached small histogram snapshot in the eval job output (see link) — mass of scores around 0.88-0.94 shift left by ~0.01

jess: did you run with same random seed & batch size? KV cache or batching can affect rounding of softmax if implementation differs

maria: seeds pinned. batch sizes: float eval used b=64, quant eval CI used b=128 to speed up. Will rerun b=64.

alex: also try +/- temperature or score rescale calibration (linear mapping) before computing MRR to see if it's a scale effect

sophia: propose quick AB: 1) rerun holdout with same batching + b=64, 2) run with canonical candidate order & dedup, 3) run evaluation with rescaling template `score' = a*score + b` fit on small calibration set

maria: ok I'll run 1,2 today. if still repro, we can run tiny per-query perturbation to see tie sensitivity.

deploy-bot: CI job build/7890 triggered by @maria: `rerank-eval-asym8-b64` — logs: https://ci.redwood/jobs/7890

dan: if it's persistent, maybe try PTQ with symmetric vs asymmetric or per-channel quantization toggle — those can change monotonicity

maria: thanks — will update here with b=64 results. if we can't resolve quickly, revert rollout and keep canary at 5% until triage complete :thumbsup:

jess: super. if helpful I can run an offline calibration (isotonic + linear) and share script

maria: appreciate it — tagging @sophia and @alex for followups.
